narratives.profile_risk: 82-year-old woman readmitted after a heart failure hospitalization that ended 2 days before start of care, with atrial fibrillation on an anticoagulant, type 2 diabetes, CKD stage 3, impaired vision and a fall in the past 3 months. She lives alone; her daughter visits weekly. SN fell short in weeks 3 and 5 and PT in weeks 4-5, and no SN or PT visits are scheduled for the rest of the period. Risk Rationale: Baseline risk is high due to the recent HF hospitalization, exertional dyspnea, polypharmacy with an anticoagulant and fall history in a patient who lives alone. Care gaps - missed SN visits during a period of weight gain and zero future skilled visits - raise hospitalization risk by reducing clinical surveillance of fluid status and medication safety.
narratives.vitals_trajectory: Ten vitals days in 33 days. No readings since DAY+33 and no SN visit scheduled. Weight alert on DAY+29 has no documented physician notification. CQI recommends a same-day phone check and MD notification.
narratives.care_delivery: Week 1 front-loading was met for SN and PT. SN fell short in weeks 3 and 5 and PT in weeks 4-5; neither shortfall was made up. The OT evaluation ordered for week 2 and the PRN MSW consult have no visit record. Schedule: Seven ordered visits remain in weeks 6-9 (4 SN, 3 PT) and none are scheduled; only HHA visits are on the calendar.
narratives.missed_care: Missed Care Impact: Two SN visits (DAY+17 patient not home; DAY+31 patient requested reschedule) and one PT visit (DAY+26 staff availability) were missed and not made up. The DAY+31 SN miss came two days after a weight alert with no documented physician notification, so a key chance to assess fluid status was lost. The OT evaluation and PRN MSW consult have no visit record. For a patient who lives alone with impaired vision, these gaps matter more than the visit count suggests.
narratives.delay_impact: ACUITYSTATUS: Acuity level 2 requires the first visit within 48 hours; the first SN visit occurred on DAY+1, within the window. Delay impact is rated moderate because later SN gaps coincided with a rising weight trend rather than because of the start-of-care timing.
narratives.data_gaps: OT evaluation ordered for week 2 has no visit, missed-visit record or cancellation.|Weight alert on DAY+29 has no physician-notification record and no follow-up note.|Pulse oximeter is listed as a needed supply but no delivery or in-home documentation was found.|Edema noted on DAY+33 has no measurement or comparison to baseline.|Living situation says the daughter visits weekly but no caregiver contact or availability is recorded.|Apixaban teaching is marked partial on DAY+15 with no later update.

medications.summary: 11 active medications including two high-risk: apixaban (bleeding risk) and insulin glargine (hypoglycemia). Understanding checked on 2 of 7 SN visits, last DAY+10. Missed doses reported DAY+15 and DAY+22; impaired vision makes labels hard to read.

care_review.assessments_summary: SN completed cardiopulmonary and edema assessments at every SN visit and medication review twice. Fall-risk (MAHC-10) was done at SOC only. Pain and depression screens were done at SOC and not repeated. No home-safety assessment has been documented because the OT evaluation was not delivered.
care_review.interventions_summary: Most interventions targeted HF self-management: HF teaching (5 visits), daily-weight teaching (3), medication teaching (3) and gait/transfer training by PT (6). Anticoagulant bleeding-precaution teaching was documented once. No intervention addressed the living-alone risk, and no diuretic or weight-escalation intervention was documented after the DAY+29 weight alert.
